h1: The 6 Best Gas Backpack Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Gas Backpack Leaf Blowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six gas backpack leaf blowers from Husqvarna, HASANEN, HTK, PROYAMA and Thalorus, with airflow figures and what each costs you.
summary: The Husqvarna 150BT is the best all-round gas backpack blower here, with the 570BTS as the step-up model. The HASANEN lists the highest airflow at 850 CFM for a lower price tier, while the HTK and Thalorus sit in the middle.
intro: Gas backpack blowers get judged on CFM, but airflow is only half the story. The hidden tradeoff is that the biggest numbers often come from lesser-known brands with thinner spec sheets, while the proven names list almost no figures at all.
We reviewed six gas backpack blowers and ranked them on the listed specifications: airflow, wind speed, engine size and price tier. Where a listing gives no number, we say so.

products.name: Husqvarna 150BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A backpack-format Husqvarna that balances proven name and price tier.
products.description:
The 150BT is a gas backpack blower from Husqvarna, listed in the $200 to $500 tier.

It ranks first because it combines the backpack format with an established brand, ahead of lesser-known models with bigger claimed airflow. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no CFM or MPH figure to compare.

Buy it if brand support matters. The caveat is the missing numbers.
products.idealFor: Buyers who value a proven brand.

products.name: Husqvarna 570BTS Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The step-up Husqvarna backpack, in the $500+ tier.
products.description:
The 570BTS is Husqvarna's backpack blower listed in the $500+ tier.

It ranks second because it costs far more than the 150BT while the listing offers no extra numbers to justify it on paper.

Choose it if you want the step-up model. The caveat is price.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the premium Husqvarna.

products.name: HASANEN Backpack Gas Powered Leaf Blower
products.description:
The HASANEN lists 850 CFM in a backpack gas format at the $50 to $100 tier, the highest airflow number here.

It ranks third because the figure is the manufacturer's listing and the brand is less proven than Husqvarna.

Buy it for big airflow on a budget. The caveat is brand support.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want maximum airflow.

products.name: HTK Backpack Blower
products.verdict: 665 CFM and 205 MPH in the middle price tier.
products.description:
The HTK lists 665 CFM and 205 MPH as a backpack blower, in the $100 to $200 tier.

It ranks fourth because its airflow is below the HASANEN while costing more, but it lists both CFM and MPH.

It suits mid-size yards. The caveat is the price versus the HASANEN.

products.name: Thalorus 52cc Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 52cc engine with 550 CFM and 230 MPH.
products.description:
The Thalorus uses a 52cc gas engine and lists 550 CFM and 230 MPH, the highest wind speed here, in the $100 to $200 tier.

It ranks fifth because the airflow is the lowest of the numbered backpack picks, though speed helps lift wet leaves.

Choose it for speed. The caveat is lower CFM.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer high wind speed.

products.name: PROYAMA 72CC Gas Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 72cc engine with few other figures listed.
products.description:
The PROYAMA lists a 72cc gas engine in a backpack format at the $100 to $200 tier.

It ranks last because no airflow or speed figure is listed, so it cannot be compared on paper with the HTK or Thalorus.

It suits buyers who want a large engine. The caveat is the thin listing.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a big engine.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is the volume of air moved, and it decides how fast you clear piles. Check the listing for the number, not a vague power claim.
MPH is the speed of the air, which lifts stuck leaves. Together with CFM it shows real clearing power. Look for both in the title.
Engine cc shows displacement. A larger engine is not always stronger. Check CFM and MPH too.
Established brands usually offer easier service. Check the brand before buying.
A backpack puts weight on your shoulders, which matters for large yards. Confirm backpack in the title.

finalTake: The Husqvarna 150BT is the safest gas backpack blower here. The HASANEN is the bargain for airflow, and the Thalorus leads on wind speed. The 570BTS is for those who want the premium model.
